panels.title: Produced today
panels.description: enphase_energy_produced_today_watt_hours / 1000 — the gateway's own since-midnight accumulator, divided by 1000 to display kWh (unit conversion belongs in the query layer, not the exporter). The metric resets to 0 at local midnight, which is exactly why it's a Gauge and not a Counter. Surprising: 0 or 'No data' mid-morning means the array, the CT metering, or the daemon is out — cross-check the Health SLI panel before blaming the panels on the roof.

panels.title: Consumed today
panels.description: enphase_energy_consumed_today_watt_hours / 1000 — the gateway's since-midnight consumption accumulator in kWh (CT-metered gateways only; if this shows 'No data' the exporter deliberately publishes nothing rather than a fake zero). Fallback if the accumulator ever disappears from pyenphase: sum_over_time(enphase_consumption_watts[24h:15s]) * 15 / 3600000 — a Riemann sum in PromQL, approximate because it integrates 15s power samples instead of reading the meter. Surprising: consumed today far above produced today on a sunny day means a heavy load ran off-solar — check the grid-import stat.

panels.title: Solar coverage (24h)
panels.description: enphase:solar_coverage_24h:ratio * 100 — a recording rule (the colons are the tell that this series is derived, not scraped): 1 minus grid-import energy over consumption energy for the trailing 24h, precomputed every minute so this panel costs one sample lookup instead of a 24h subquery per refresh (materialized view for the observability stack). Reads as 'what fraction of the house's energy did NOT come from the grid'. Unhealthy: red under 30% on a sunny day means solar+battery barely offset the house — sizing problem, heavy new load, or the battery mode is fighting you.

panels.title: Grid flow now
panels.description: enphase_grid_import_watts and enphase_grid_export_watts — the exporter splits the gateway's one signed net-consumption reading into two always-non-negative directional gauges (directional gauges over signed values: easier to stack, threshold, and rate() than a signed series). Positive on both sides is impossible by construction; whichever is nonzero tells you which way electrons are flowing right now. Surprising: importing during peak sun means a load spike or a battery refusing to discharge — check mode and SoC.

panels.title: Solar vs Consumption
panels.description: Two raw gauges plotted over time: enphase_production_watts (what the panels are making) and enphase_consumption_watts (what the house is using). No PromQL operators needed — gauges are instantaneous values, so plotting the raw series IS the query. Unhealthy: production flatlining at 0 during daylight (array or gateway problem), or either series going stale/gappy (daemon or Prometheus down — cross-check the Health SLI panel).

panels.title: Battery SoC
panels.description: enphase_battery_soc_ratio * 100 — the exporter publishes state of charge as a 0-1 ratio (Prometheus naming convention), and the `* 100` scalar multiplication converts it to percent for display. Unhealthy: red below 20% (approaching the backup floor — the battery can no longer ride out an outage), yellow below 40%.

panels.title: Scrape freshness + error rate
panels.description: The service-health (SLI) panel — this is where an SLO would hang, e.g. 'state age under 60s for 99% of 30 days'. Series 1: enphase_state_age_seconds, seconds since the last successful gateway read; with a 15s scrape loop it should hover near 15. Yellow past 30s, red past 60s means the daemon is being served stale cache (gateway down, breaker open). Series 2: rate(enphase_scrape_total{outcome="error"}[5m]) — `rate()` converts the ever-increasing error counter into errors-per-second averaged over a sliding 5-minute window; healthy is a flat line at 0. Age climbing while error rate stays 0 means the daemon itself died (Prometheus will also mark the target down).

panels.title: Time in each mode (24h)
panels.description: enphase:time_in_mode_24h:seconds — a recording rule implementing the info-gauge-integrated-over-time pattern. The mode gauge enphase_battery_mode{mode=...} is 1 while a mode is active, 0 otherwise; sum_over_time at a 15s subquery step multiplied by 15 is a Riemann sum giving seconds spent in each mode over the last 24h, one slice per mode label. Surprising: any slice for full_backup you didn't ask for (something flipped the battery to backup — check the writes audit counter), or a mode split that doesn't match your schedule (rules engine and reality disagree).
